items.note: Object code alone needs no notice

items.label: Apache-2.0
items.note: Adds a patent grant and a trademark carve-out

items.label: 0BSD, MIT-0
items.note: Permission only

items.label: Unlicense, CC0-1.0
items.note: CC0 keeps the affirmer's patent and mark rights

points: **Notice condition:** MIT and ISC give the permission only if the notice appears in all copies (MIT, full text; ISC, full text).
**Binary distribution:** BSD-2-Clause repeats the notice for binary distribution, while BSL-1.0 exempts object code generated by a source language processor (BSD-2-Clause cl.2; BSL-1.0 full text).
**Zlib:** Zlib keeps the notice in source distributions, requires altered source to be plainly marked, and bars misrepresenting origin (zlib License cl.1-3).
**Apache-2.0:** Notice, changed-file and NOTICE duties apply on distribution. The licence adds an express patent grant and a trademark carve-out (Apache-2.0 s.3, s.4, s.6).
**Standardise:** Keep a short approved list of licence texts, so that engineers do not create variants by accident (good practice).

deepDive.heading: Compliance follows the artefact you ship
deepDive.lede: Duties attach to copies that leave the bank's control, so the shipped artefact sets the compliance task.

items.label: Identify shipped components
items.note: Use the bill of materials for each release

items.label: Place notices in the artefact
items.note: Licence and notice files inside the app bundle, image or package

items.label: Check Apache extras
items.note: Changed-file marks, and NOTICE text where users see attributions

items.label: Confirm whether copies leave
items.note: Internal copies still need the MIT and ISC notices, and only copies sent to others trigger the distribution duties

points: **Mobile apps:** Installing an app on a customer's device distributes object code, so notices must reach the user, typically in a licence screen or bundled file (drafting inference; BSD-2-Clause cl.2).
**Container images:** A pushed image copies its layers to others, so put the licence and notice files inside the image, not only in the source repository (drafting inference).

**Hosted services:** The permissive texts attach duties to copies, and Apache-2.0 s.4 attaches them to distribution. Running code on your own servers and serving results to users sends no copies of the code (drafting inference).
**Client code:** Scripts, SDKs or libraries sent to a browser or device are distributed, even when the hosted service that uses them is not (drafting inference).

**Apache attribution:** Apache-2.0 s.4(d) requires the [[NOTICE file]] text in one of three places: a NOTICE file in the distribution, the source or documentation, or a display where third-party notices normally appear, such as an about screen (Apache-2.0 s.4(d)).

deepDive.heading: Stripping notices: § 1202
deepDive.lede: A deleted header can be a copyright problem as well as a licence breach.
points: **Copyright management information:** The DMCA protects [[CMI|Copyright management information]] such as the title, author, owner and terms for use, and a licence notice can fall within that definition (17 U.S.C. § 1202(c)).

**Removal rule:** Intentional removal without authority is prohibited where the person knows, or for civil claims has reasonable grounds to know, that it will induce, enable, facilitate or conceal infringement (17 U.S.C. § 1202(b)(1)).
**Distribution:** Distributing copies while knowing that the information was removed or altered without authority is also covered (17 U.S.C. § 1202(b)(3)).
**Licence headers:** Courts have accepted licence headers as copyright management information in some cases, so a header is more than decoration (reported; check).
**Civil remedies:** Anyone injured by a § 1202 violation may sue, and the court may grant injunctions (17 U.S.C. § 1203(a), (b)(1)).

**AI output:** The Ninth Circuit is reported (16 September 2026) to have affirmed dismissal of a § 1202(b) claim over AI coding output in Doe v. GitHub, Inc., rejecting a strict identicality test (reported; check).

deepDive.heading: Patents: silence in most licences, a grant in Apache
deepDive.lede: A permissive copyright licence clears the code, but it does not clear the patents that the code may practise.

visual.caption: What each source of permission covers.

items.label: MIT, ISC, BSD
items.note: No patent terms; any patent permission must be implied

items.label: Apache-2.0 s.3
items.note: From each contributor, for claims its contribution necessarily infringes

items.label: CC0-1.0 s.4(a)
items.note: Patent rights are not waived or licensed

items.label: 35 U.S.C. § 271(a)
items.note: Making, using or selling a patented invention needs authority

points: **Silence:** The MIT, ISC and BSD texts contain no patent terms, so any patent permission is implied. Do not rely on an implied patent permission for a product that practises a claimed method (good practice).

**Express grant:** Under Apache-2.0 s.3, each contributor grants a perpetual, royalty-free patent licence over the claims its contribution necessarily infringes, alone or in combination with the Work.

**Termination:** The grant ends if you start patent litigation alleging that the Work, or a contribution in it, infringes. A [[Patent termination clause]] makes the bank's own patent claims a risk to its rights in that code (Apache-2.0 s.3).
**Patent exposure:** Under 35 U.S.C. § 271(a), making, using or selling a patented invention without authority is infringement, whichever copyright licence covers the code.
**Dedication:** CC0 leaves the affirmer's patent rights untouched, so a public domain dedication does not clear patents (CC0-1.0 s.4(a)).

deepDive.heading: Names, marks and endorsement
deepDive.lede: Licences grant rights in code. They do not grant the right to use a brand.
points: **Lanham Act:** Using a name in a way likely to suggest sponsorship, approval or affiliation can be a false designation of origin (15 U.S.C. § 1125(a)(1)(A)).
**BSD-3-Clause:** Bars using the copyright holder's or contributors' names to endorse or promote derived products without prior written permission ([[Non-endorsement clause]]; BSD-3-Clause cl.3).
**Apache-2.0:** Gives no permission to use the Licensor's trade names or marks, beyond describing the origin of the Work and reproducing the NOTICE file (Apache-2.0 s.6).
**Zlib:** Bars misrepresenting altered software as the original, and requires altered source to be plainly marked (zlib License cl.2).

**Use in commerce:** Federal mark claims reach only infringing use in commerce in the US (Abitron Austria GmbH v. Hetronic International, Inc., 600 U.S. 412 (2023)), so a copy in a foreign fork is a separate question (drafting inference).

deepDive.heading: Licence variants and proliferation
deepDive.lede: Small edits to standard text create new licences, and each one needs its own review.

items.label: Identify the licence
items.note: Read the file header, LICENSE file and package metadata

items.label: Compare with the standard text
items.note: Check each clause against the published text

items.label: Test the new terms
items.note: Look for use limits, patent or name terms and changed notices

items.label: Approve or refuse
items.note: Record the decision against the component and version

points: **Proliferation:** Projects often tweak MIT or BSD text, add clauses or write their own. Treat each variant as a new licence, not a synonym (good practice).

**Use limits:** The OSI Open Source Definition bars licences that discriminate against persons, groups or fields of endeavour. A use restriction can therefore take a licence outside that definition (a view, not law).
**Named variants:** Variants such as the JSON licence are MIT-style texts with added terms, so read the full text, not the name (drafting inference).
**Identifiers:** Record each licence by its [[SPDX identifier]], the standard set in ISO/IEC 5962:2021, so that scans, approvals and the register use one vocabulary.
**Apache changes:** Apache-2.0 s.4 lets a distributor add its own terms to its modifications, provided it meets the Work's conditions (Apache-2.0 s.4).
**Compatibility:** The FSF treats Apache-2.0 as compatible with GPLv3 but not GPLv2. That is the FSF's view, not a court ruling.

provisions.title: Subject matter of copyright; ideas excluded
provisions.summary: Copyright protects original works of authorship fixed in a tangible medium, which covers code. Section 102(b) denies protection to any idea, procedure, process, system, method of operation or concept, however the work describes it.
provisions.counselNote: A licence grants permission under copyright. It cannot give rights in an idea or method, so for an idea or method a patent is the usual route, and a trade secret may protect what stays confidential (drafting inference).

provisions.title: Exclusive rights of the copyright owner
provisions.summary: The owner may reproduce the work, prepare derivative works, distribute copies, and perform or display the work publicly, and may authorise others to do these acts.
provisions.counselNote: A permissive licence is an authorisation of these acts. Anything outside its grant stays with the owner.

provisions.title: Writing required for transfers of ownership
provisions.summary: A transfer of copyright ownership, other than by operation of law, is not valid unless it is in writing and signed by the owner of the rights conveyed or its agent.
provisions.counselNote: A permissive licence is not a transfer, so it needs no signed writing. An assignment of code from a contractor does need one.

provisions.title: Copyright management information
provisions.summary: Bars intentional removal or alteration of copyright management information without authority, where the person knows, or for civil claims has reasonable grounds to know, that it will facilitate infringement. Distributing copies knowing the information was removed is also covered.
provisions.counselNote: Deleting licence headers or copyright notices to conceal copying carries a separate civil claim. Counsel should treat deliberate stripping in build pipelines as a control failure.

provisions.title: False designation of origin and false endorsement
provisions.summary: Prohibits using a word, name or symbol in commerce in a way likely to cause confusion about sponsorship, approval or affiliation. It covers unregistered marks as well as registered ones.
provisions.counselNote: Using a contributor's or upstream project's name in marketing can imply approval. Check the plan against BSD-3-Clause clause 3 and the Apache-2.0 trademark carve-out.

provisions.title: Infringement by making, using or selling
provisions.summary: Making, using, offering to sell, selling or importing a patented invention without authority infringes the patent. A copyright licence gives no authority under a patent.
provisions.counselNote: A permissive copyright licence does not clear patents. Code that implements a claimed method needs a separate patent review.

provisions.title: Licence terms as conditions of the copyright licence
provisions.summary: The Federal Circuit held that the attribution and change-notice terms of the Artistic License were conditions limiting the scope of the licence. A user who broke them could be sued for copyright infringement, including for an injunction, not only for breach of contract.
provisions.counselNote: The same argument can be made about MIT and BSD notice terms. A dropped notice may mean the copying was unlicensed, so keep the notices intact.

provisions.title: MIT License
provisions.summary: Permits use, copying, modification, merger, publication, distribution, sublicensing and sale. The copyright notice and permission notice must be included in all copies or substantial portions. The licence disclaims warranties and liability, and says nothing about patents or names.
provisions.counselNote: The notice is the main compliance duty. The silence on patents and names is a gap that counsel should close by policy, not by assumption.

provisions.title: Non-endorsement clause
provisions.summary: Redistribution and use are permitted with the notice and disclaimer retained in source, and in binary form too. Clause 3 bars using the copyright holder's or contributors' names to endorse or promote derived products without specific prior written permission.
provisions.counselNote: The clause protects names, not code. A product launch that uses a contributor's name needs written permission, whatever the code licence says.

provisions.title: zlib License
provisions.summary: Permits any use, including commercial use, with altering and redistribution. Origin must not be misrepresented, altered source must be plainly marked, and the notice may not be removed from any source distribution. An acknowledgement is appreciated but not required.
provisions.counselNote: Zlib has a short notice rule for source distributions and no object-code duty. Teams should still check that altered versions are marked as such.

provisions.title: Boost Software License 1.0
provisions.summary: Permits use, reproduction, display, distribution and derivative works. The copyright notices and the licence must be included in all copies in source, and in derivative works, unless the copy is solely machine-executable object code generated by a source language processor.
provisions.counselNote: Compiled products can ship without the notice text in the object code. The source and documentation trail still needs to keep it.

provisions.title: Grant of Patent License
provisions.summary: Each contributor grants a perpetual, royalty-free patent licence over the patent claims its contribution necessarily infringes, alone or in combination with the Work. The licence for that Work ends if you sue alleging that the Work or a contribution infringes a patent.
provisions.counselNote: This is the only short permissive text here with an express patent grant. Its termination clause is a litigation trigger for the bank when it is the patent owner.

provisions.title: Redistribution conditions
provisions.summary: A distributor must give recipients a copy of the licence, mark modified files, keep the notices of the Work, and carry the attribution text of any NOTICE file in a place where users can see it. The distributor may add its own terms to its own modifications.
provisions.counselNote: Each condition becomes a release task. Missing one can take a redistribution outside the licence, so the release team needs a checklist.

provisions.title: Limitations and disclaimers: patent and trademark rights
provisions.summary: No trademark or patent rights held by the affirmer are waived, abandoned, surrendered, licensed or otherwise affected by the dedication. The affirmer also disclaims warranties.
provisions.counselNote: A public domain dedication still leaves patents in place. CC0 code can therefore carry patent risk even though it has no copyright conditions.

checklist: **Inventory components:** Record each permissive component, its version, SPDX identifier and notice file for every shipped product (good practice).
**Ship the notices:** Put licence texts and copyright notices inside every app bundle, container image and SDK package, and confirm them in the build output (good practice).
**Approve known texts only:** Accept the standard SPDX texts on the policy list, and send any edited or custom licence to counsel as a new licence.
**Meet Apache-2.0 duties:** Confirm that a licence copy travels with each distribution, changed files are marked, and NOTICE text appears where users see attributions (Apache-2.0 s.4).
**Clear patents separately:** Do not treat a permissive copyright licence as patent clearance. Route code that implements claimed methods to patent review (good practice).
**Check the patent trigger:** Before the bank sues over a patent, check whether the accused product uses Apache-2.0 code, because suing over the Work ends that licence (Apache-2.0 s.3).
**Keep names out of launches:** Do not use an upstream project's or contributor's name to promote a bank product without written permission (BSD-3-Clause cl.3; 15 U.S.C. § 1125(a)).
**Guard notices in pipelines:** Require review before any tool removes licence headers, and treat deliberate removal as a possible § 1202 issue (17 U.S.C. § 1202(b)).
**Review forks and variants:** Treat a renamed fork, or a licence with changed wording, as a new approval request, even when most of the text is standard (good practice).
**Record approvals:** Log the approver, date and scope for each permissive component, so an audit can match a release to its terms (good practice).
itAngle: **Scanners read identifiers:** Licence scanners match SPDX identifiers and notice text, so a clean scan does not prove that the shipped binary carries the notices (good practice).

**Copy notices in the build:** Add a build step that copies LICENSE and NOTICE files into each artefact, such as an app bundle, container layer, wheel or npm package, and fails if one is missing (good practice).

**Keep banners through minification:** Bundlers and minifiers can drop comments, including licence banners. Configure them to keep licence comments, and check the minified output (drafting inference).
**Vendored copies lose context:** Copying a file into a repository separates it from its upstream licence file. Keep the licence beside vendored code and record the upstream version (good practice).
**Trace each release:** Keep a record of which component versions and licence texts each release used, so that an audit can show which terms governed a given build (good practice).
virtualBankNotes: **Third-party guidance:** The interagency third-party guidance (88 Fed. Reg. 37920, 9 June 2023) is technology-neutral. Open source components are usually not the business arrangement, but the vendors that supply or support them are (drafting inference).
**FFIEC booklet:** The FFIEC IT Examination Handbook's development and acquisition booklet is reported to cover open source components in supply-chain risk (reported; check the booklet's wording).

**NYDFS rules:** For entities regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services, 23 NYCRR 500.8 covers written secure development procedures for in-house applications and for evaluating the security of externally developed applications, and 500.11 covers a third-party service provider security policy.
**Inventory expectations:** PCI DSS is an industry standard, not a statute. Its requirement 6.3.2 asks for an inventory of bespoke software and third-party components (reported; check).
**Vendor deliverables:** Where a vendor ships permissive code in its product, ask for the notice file and component list in the delivery, since those are compliance evidence (good practice).
productNotes: **Treat permissive code as a copyright clearance only:** A permissive licence does not clear third-party patents that the code may practise (35 U.S.C. § 271(a)). Apache-2.0 s.3 gives only a limited patent grant from each contributor, for patent claims that its own contribution necessarily infringes (Apache-2.0 s.3). Route code that implements a claimed method to patent review before it ships (good practice).

**Ship the notices in every artefact:** Put the licence text and notice files inside each app bundle, container image and SDK. If the Apache-2.0 work includes a NOTICE file, put its attribution text where users see attributions, such as an about screen, or in another place s.4(d) allows (Apache-2.0 s.4(d)).

**Keep contributor names out of launches:** Marketing must not use the names of an upstream copyright holder or its contributors to endorse or promote a bank product derived from that code without written permission (BSD-3-Clause cl.3). A project's own name is a trademark question (15 U.S.C. § 1125(a)(1)(A)).

**Send edited licences to counsel as new ones:** A tweaked MIT or BSD text, or a licence with added clauses, can change the conditions, so raise it with counsel before the code merges (good practice).
pitfalls: **Dropping notices:** Treating MIT or BSD code as free of duties and stripping its notice. If the notice is a licence condition, the copying may be infringement, not just a breach (Jacobsen v. Katzer, 535 F.3d 1373 (Fed. Cir. 2008)).
**Patent trap:** Suing a partner over a patent while relying on Apache-2.0 code it uses, because the licence for that Work can end (Apache-2.0 s.3).

**Implied patent licence:** Assuming an implied patent permission in MIT or BSD code survives an acquisition. Non-exclusive patent licences are generally personal and cannot be assigned without consent unless the licence allows it (In re CFLC, Inc., 89 F.3d 673 (9th Cir. 1996)). That case concerned express patent licences, so applying it to MIT or BSD code is a drafting inference.
**Name use in launches:** Using an upstream project's name or logo in product marketing in a way that suggests approval (15 U.S.C. § 1125(a); BSD-3-Clause cl.3).
**Silent variants:** Accepting a renamed licence whose text changed one clause, which can change the conditions or the open source status (drafting inference).
**Hosted services as safe:** Treating a hosted service as free of duties when the client code and SDKs sent to users are distributed (drafting inference).

points: **AI model copyright policy:** a general-purpose AI model provider must have a copyright policy and publish a training-content summary (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 53(1)(c)-(d)).
**Open-source models:** they are exempt only from the documentation duties in Art. 53(1)(a)-(b) (Art. 53(2)), not from the copyright duties.

**Broadly the same:** no UK rule specific to the notices of a permissive licence is identified, so the notices are read as ordinary copyright permissions with conditions, since programs are literary works (CDPA 1988 s.3(1)(b)) (drafting inference).
**Model training:** a trained model was not an 'infringing copy' in Getty Images v Stability AI [2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch), 4 November 2025; permission to appeal was granted (reported; check).

**Attribution waivers, not assignments:** moral rights, including the right to be named, may be waived but not assigned (Copyright Act s.14.1(2)), so contributor or credit terms should be drafted as waivers; check with Canadian counsel.
**Broadly the same otherwise:** no separate Canadian rule for permissive licence notices is identified here (drafting inference; check).

hongKong.summary: Hong Kong treats a permissive licence as a copyright permission and a contract, with no separate regime for notices. Two points stand out: removing rights management information gives only a civil remedy, with no criminal offence of the US kind, and only against a person who knows or has reason to believe the act induces, enables, facilitates or conceals infringement (Cap. 528 s.274(2A)), and Apache-2.0's patent grant is not limited to one jurisdiction, so it reaches a Hong Kong patent that a contributor owns over its contribution (Apache-2.0 s.3).
keyPoints: **Permission, not transfer:** A permissive licence authorises the restricted acts it names, and the copyright itself stays with the author (Cap. 528 s.22(1)-(2); drafting inference).

**Notices:** Removing or altering electronic rights management information without authority gives copyright-type remedies only against a person who knows or has reason to believe the act induces, enables, facilitates or conceals infringement (Cap. 528 s.274(2), (2A)).

**Knowledge for third-party code:** Possessing or distributing an infringing copy in a trade or business is secondary infringement only where the person knows or has reason to believe the copy is infringing (Cap. 528 s.31(1)(a)-(c)).

**Patents:** A copyright licence does not clear patents. Among the common permissive texts, only Apache-2.0 has an express patent grant (Apache-2.0 s.3), and Hong Kong patents follow the Patents Ordinance (drafting inference).
**Counsel's job:** Approve only known licence texts, and make sure the notice reaches every app, image and SDK the bank ships (good practice).

sections.heading: Notices and the copies the bank ships
sections.lede: The licence's notice term attaches to copies, so the shipped artefact decides what the bank must include.
points: **Copies in any material form:** Copying covers reproduction in any material form, including electronic storage, and copies made in passing count (Cap. 528 s.23(2), (6)).

**Issue to the public:** Putting copies into circulation includes doing so in electronic form (Cap. 528 s.24(2), (4)). An app or SDK that customers download is therefore a distribution (drafting inference).

**Stripping notices:** A person who removes or alters electronic rights management information without authority has copyright-type remedies against them only where the act induces, enables, facilitates or conceals infringement and the person knows or has reason to believe it (Cap. 528 s.274(2)(a), (2A)).

**What counts:** Information that identifies the work, its author or owner, or its terms of use counts when it is attached to a copy (Cap. 528 s.274(3)(a)-(b)). A copyright or licence header in a source file often does this, so it is more than decoration (drafting inference).
sections.takeaway: Keep the notice inside each shipped artefact, including the app's licence screen and the container image, and do not strip headers when copying code into a product (good practice).

sections.heading: Third-party code and knowledge
sections.lede: Liability for an infringing copy turns on what the bank knew or had reason to believe about it.
points: **Trade possession and distribution:** Possessing, selling or distributing an infringing copy in the course of a trade or business is infringement only where the person knows or has reason to believe the copy is infringing (Cap. 528 s.31(1)(a)-(c), (2)).
**Distribution outside trade:** Distribution outside trade counts only where it affects the owner prejudicially, judged by the factors in s.31(3) (Cap. 528 s.31(1)(d), (3)).
**Authorising others:** A person who authorises another to do a restricted act infringes, and the court may weigh that person's control and any reasonable steps to stop it (Cap. 528 s.22(2), (2A)).

**Porting permissive code:** Porting a permissive library to another language is an adaptation (Cap. 528 s.29(3)(b), (4)). The permissive licence itself permits that; without it, a lawful user may adapt only where that is necessary for lawful use (Cap. 528 s.61(1)).
sections.takeaway: Record how each third-party component came into the bank, because knowledge or reason to believe is the test for liability (good practice).

sections.heading: Patents and the Apache-2.0 grant
sections.lede: A copyright licence does not clear patents, and the Apache-2.0 patent grant carries its own termination trap.
points: **Express grant:** Under Apache-2.0 s.3, each contributor grants a patent licence that is not limited to one jurisdiction. It covers claims the contribution necessarily infringes, alone or in combination with the Work (Apache-2.0 s.3).

**Termination trap:** The grant ends if the licensee sues alleging that the Work infringes a patent (Apache-2.0 s.3). A patent claim by the bank over the code can therefore end its rights in that code.

**Short-term patents:** A short-term patent is granted after formality examination only, and lasts up to 8 years from filing, subject to a renewal fee at the end of year 4 (Cap. 514 ss.117, 126(1)(b), (2)).
sections.takeaway: Add the Apache-2.0 termination clause to the bank's patent-litigation approval, so that no team starts a patent claim without knowing it can end its rights in the code (good practice).

provisions.title: Issue of copies to the public, including electronic copies
provisions.summary: Issuing copies to the public means putting into circulation copies not previously circulated, by or with the consent of the owner. It includes issuing the original and issuing copies in electronic form.
provisions.counselNote: Shipping a permissive component to customers in an app or SDK is an issue of copies, so the notice must travel with it.

provisions.title: Secondary infringement: dealing with an infringing copy
provisions.summary: Possessing, selling, distributing or exhibiting an infringing copy in trade or business infringes only where the person knows or has reason to believe the copy is infringing. Distribution outside trade counts only where it affects the owner prejudicially, judged by listed factors.
provisions.counselNote: A bank that receives third-party code in breach of its licence is not caught unless it has that knowledge or reason to believe. Its intake records therefore matter.

provisions.title: Rights management information: remedies and knowledge
provisions.summary: A person who provides rights management information has the same remedies as a copyright owner against anyone who removes or alters it without authority, but only where that person knows or has reason to believe the act induces, enables, facilitates or conceals infringement. The information must identify the work, its author or owner, or its terms of use.
provisions.counselNote: The remedy depends on knowledge and on the content of the notice. A standard licence header is the usual case, so keeping headers intact is the simplest protection.

provisions.title: Short-term patent: formality examination only
provisions.summary: The Registrar of Patents, when examining an application for a short-term patent, is not required to consider patentability, priority entitlement or proper disclosure, among other matters.
provisions.counselNote: A short-term patent gives less assurance than a standard patent that has been substantively examined. A bank should not treat one as clearance for a method the code practises.

provisions.title: Term of a short-term patent
provisions.summary: A short-term patent remains in force until the end of 8 years beginning with the date of filing the application, subject to the renewal provisions in s.126(2) and (3).
provisions.counselNote: The term is far shorter than the term of a standard patent, so a patent that matters to the product may have expired or may still be running on a timetable the bank should check.

bankNotes: **Vendor deliverables:** Ask a vendor that ships permissive components for the notice file and component list with each delivery, because the bank needs them to meet its licence duties (good practice).

**Personal data in hosted components:** Where a permissive component runs in the bank's systems and a third party hosts or supports it while processing customer personal data, the bank must adopt contractual or other means to protect that data (Cap. 486 Sch. 1, DPP 4(2)).

**Customer terms:** An MIT or Apache disclaimer protects the licensor, not the bank. The bank's own app terms cannot exclude liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, and other exclusions of negligence liability, or of contract liability against a consumer or on the bank's standard terms, must be reasonable, which the bank must prove (Cap. 71 s.3(6), s.7, s.8; drafting inference).

glossary.definition: A licence that lets users copy, modify and redistribute code on light conditions, usually a notice requirement with no duty to release changes. MIT, BSD, ISC and Apache-2.0 are examples (MIT, full text).
A licence that leaves the owner free to license the same rights to others. It is not a transfer of ownership, so the signed-writing rule in 17 U.S.C. § 204(a) does not apply to it.
Identifying information conveyed with a work, such as its title, author, owner and terms for use. Intentional removal without authority can breach 17 U.S.C. § 1202(b) (§ 1202(c)).

An optional text file in an Apache-2.0 work that carries attribution notices. A distributor must include its attribution text in a NOTICE file, in the source or documentation, or in a display where third-party notices normally appear (Apache-2.0 s.4(d)).
A licence term that bars using the authors' or contributors' names to endorse or promote derived products without written permission (BSD-3-Clause cl.3).
A licence term that ends a patent licence if the licensee sues alleging that the work or a contribution infringes a patent (Apache-2.0 s.3).
A waiver of copyright, such as CC0 or the Unlicense, that leaves other rights in place. CC0 says that the affirmer's patent and trademark rights are not affected (CC0-1.0 s.4(a)).
A standard short name for a licence, such as MIT or Apache-2.0, set out in the SPDX standard (ISO/IEC 5962:2021).
A licence that changes standard wording, adds clauses or uses a new name. Each variant needs its own review because its conditions may differ.
A licence such as 0BSD or MIT-0 that grants permission without requiring that a notice be kept (0BSD, full text; MIT-0, full text).

A Hong Kong patent granted after formality examination only, which lasts up to 8 years from filing if renewed at year 4 (Cap. 514 ss.117, 126(1)(b), (2)). It differs from a standard patent, which is granted after substantive examination.
Information that identifies a work, its author or owner, or its terms of use, when it is attached to a copy or appears with a communication of the work to the public (Cap. 528 s.274(3)).

title: Copyleft licences
oneLiner: Copyleft duties start when the bank conveys code to others, and they reach the whole work it distributes, so scope comes first.
keyPoints: For GPL, LGPL and MPL code, the duties arise when the bank conveys copies to others (network copyleft is covered separately). Running software inside the bank, or letting users reach it over a network, is not [[conveying|conveying]] under GPL-3.0 (GPL-3.0 s.0).

**Strong copyleft:** A work based on GPL code, when distributed, must be licensed as a whole under the GPL (GPL-2.0 s.2(b); GPL-3.0 s.5(c)). Mere aggregation on a shared medium does not spread the licence (GPL-2.0 s.2).

**Weak copyleft:** LGPL lets a combined work carry the distributor's own terms if the recipient can relink or replace the library and reverse engineer for debugging (LGPL-2.1 s.6; LGPL-3.0 s.4). MPL-2.0 is file-level, so a [[Larger Work|Larger Work]] may carry other terms (MPL-2.0 s.3.3).

**Source duty:** Each binary must come with its [[Corresponding Source|Corresponding Source]], or with a written offer valid for at least three years (GPL-2.0 s.3(b)). Under GPL-3.0 the written offer is allowed only for object code in a physical product; a download needs equivalent access to the source, which may sit on another server if clear directions point to it (GPL-3.0 s.6(b), (d)). Installation information duties apply only when object code is conveyed in a User Product (in essence a consumer product) and possession and use pass to the recipient (GPL-3.0 s.6).

**Breach:** GPL-2.0 s.4 ends the licence on any breach, and the text gives no cure period. GPL-3.0 s.8 permanently reinstates a licensee who cures within 30 days after receiving the first notice from that copyright holder (GPL-3.0 s.8).
**Counsel's role:** Make copyleft a release gate. Confirm which code is conveyed, to whom and in which form, before each release (good practice).

deepDive.heading: The copyleft duty reaches the whole work
deepDive.lede: A strong copyleft licence spreads through the distributed work, not just the code it covers.

visual.caption: The duty grows with what is combined and then distributed.

items.label: Copyleft program
items.note: The program as licensed

items.label: Work based on the program
items.note: Modified or combined code

items.label: Distribution to others
items.note: Copies leave the bank

items.label: Whole work under the GPL
items.note: At no charge to third parties

points: **Derivative works:** A work based on the program, when distributed, must be licensed as a whole under the GPL, at no charge to all third parties (GPL-2.0 s.2(b)).
**Same test in GPL-3.0:** The whole work is licensed under GPL-3.0, along with any section 7 additional terms, however its parts are packaged (GPL-3.0 s.5(c)).

**Aggregates:** Mere aggregation on a storage or distribution medium does not bring other works under the GPL (GPL-2.0 s.2). Under GPL-3.0 the aggregate label is lost if the compilation limits users' rights beyond what the individual works permit (GPL-3.0 s.5).

**Linking:** Whether linking creates a derivative work is unsettled in US courts (17 U.S.C. § 106(2)). The FSF treats static and dynamic linking as creating a combined work, a view no US court has adopted (FSF view).
**Design choice:** Where copyleft code meets bank code is an architecture question. Engineering should record that boundary before the licence scope is decided (good practice).
deepDive.takeaway: Map where copyleft code meets proprietary code before deciding whether the product is one work.

deepDive.heading: Distribution triggers the duty, not use
deepDive.lede: Running software inside the bank is not conveying. Giving a copy to someone else is.

visual.caption: Shipping a binary built with GPL code, in order.

items.label: Decide whether the bank conveys
items.note: A copy to a third party, or to a group company treated as distribution

items.label: Provide the source
items.note: Source, a written offer or access from a designated place

items.label: License the whole work
items.note: Work based on the program

items.label: Keep the notices
items.note: Modified-file and licence notices

items.label: Respond to any notice
items.note: Cure within 30 days of the first notice

points: **Internal use:** Mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not [[conveying|conveying]] (GPL-3.0 s.0). The FSF says copying within one organisation is not distribution (FSF view).

**Group companies:** The FSF says that whether moving a copy to a majority-owned, controlled subsidiary is distribution turns on local copyright law, and that US law appears not to treat it as distribution (reported; check). Affiliates are separate legal persons, so treat transfers between them, including to a subsidiary, as distribution unless a licence term says otherwise (drafting inference).
**Contractors:** The bank may give covered works to contractors who make changes only for the bank, if those contractors cannot copy the work outside their relationship with the bank (GPL-3.0 s.2).

**Network use:** GPL-2.0 has no network clause, and GPL-3.0 treats remote interaction without a copy as not conveying (GPL-3.0 s.0). Network-triggered duties sit in the network copyleft licences covered separately.
deepDive.takeaway: Ask who receives a copy before asking which licence applies.

deepDive.heading: Source offers and installation information
deepDive.lede: The source duty comes in several listed forms, and each has its own limit.

visual.caption: How each GPL version lets the bank meet the source duty for object code.

items.label: GPL-2.0 s.3(a)
items.note: Machine-readable source on a medium customary for software interchange

items.label: GPL-2.0 s.3(b)
items.note: Valid for at least three years

items.label: GPL-2.0 s.3(c)
items.note: Noncommercial distribution only

items.label: GPL-3.0 s.6(a)-(e)
items.note: Physical medium, written offer, pass-on, designated place, or peer-to-peer

items.label: User Product
items.note: Installation information where possession and use pass to the buyer in perpetuity or for a fixed term

points: **Three years:** GPL-2.0 s.3(b) needs a written offer valid for at least three years. GPL-3.0 s.6(b) requires an offer valid for at least three years and for as long as the bank offers spare parts or customer support for that model (GPL-3.0 s.6(b)).

**Designated place:** Offering access to copy the object code from a place means offering equivalent access to the source from the same place; under GPL-3.0 the source may sit on another server if clear directions next to the object code point to it (GPL-2.0 s.3; GPL-3.0 s.6(d)).

**User Product duty:** For a [[User Product|User Product]], the buyer must receive installation information, unless no one can install modified object code on the device, as with ROM-only code (GPL-3.0 s.6).
**Scope of source:** Corresponding Source excludes System Libraries and general tools used unmodified, but includes scripts and interface definition files (GPL-3.0 s.1).
**Release practice:** Ship source with every release that includes copyleft binaries, and keep the offer or the repository live for the full period (good practice).
deepDive.takeaway: Put the source offer and its end date into the release checklist.

deepDive.heading: Weak copyleft and the exceptions
deepDive.lede: Some licences stop the duty at a library or a file. Exceptions carve out more.

visual.caption: Where each licence's duty stops, as the licence text sets it.

items.label: GPL-2.0 and GPL-3.0
items.note: A work based on the program, as a whole

items.label: LGPL-2.1 and LGPL-3.0
items.note: A combined work may keep its terms if relinking and reverse engineering are allowed

items.label: MPL-2.0
items.note: A Larger Work may carry other terms

items.label: EPL-2.0
items.note: May take a Secondary License when combined with GPL material in a separate file and the Exhibit A notice is attached

items.label: Classpath exception 2.0
items.note: Independent modules keep their own terms

points: **LGPL-2.1:** A combined work may be distributed on the distributor's own terms if they permit modification for the customer's own use and reverse engineering for debugging such modifications (LGPL-2.1 s.6).

**LGPL-3.0:** The combined work must come with the GPL and LGPL texts. The bank then either conveys minimal Corresponding Source with the application code or uses a shared library the user can replace (LGPL-3.0 s.4(d)).

**MPL-2.0:** Covered software distributed in source form stays under the MPL, and an executable must be accompanied by a way to obtain its source (MPL-2.0 s.3.1-3.2). A [[Larger Work|Larger Work]] may use other terms (MPL-2.0 s.3.3).

**Secondary licences:** Where MPL-covered software is combined with work under a [[Secondary License|Secondary License]], the covered software may also be distributed under that licence, unless it carries the Exhibit B notice (MPL-2.0 s.3.3; Exhibit B).

**Exceptions:** The [[Classpath exception|Classpath exception]] lets independent modules link with the library and keep their own terms (Classpath-exception-2.0). The LLVM exception lets embedded portions of Apache-2.0 code ship in object form without complying with sections 4(a), 4(b) and 4(d) (LLVM-exception).
deepDive.takeaway: Read the licence's exception and any file notice, not only the licence name.

deepDive.heading: Termination, cure and patents
deepDive.lede: Copyleft licences end on breach, and GPL-3.0 adds patent terms when code is conveyed.

visual.caption: The cure route under GPL-3.0 s.8 after a first notice.

items.label: Violation
items.note: Conveying or modifying outside the licence

items.label: Stop the violation
items.note: Licence reinstated provisionally

items.label: Cure within 30 days of the first notice
items.note: Reinstated permanently

items.label: No notice within 60 days
items.note: Permanent reinstatement without a notice

points: **GPL-2.0 termination:** Any attempt to copy, modify or distribute other than as the licence allows is void and ends the licence. Parties who received copies from the bank keep theirs, so long as they comply (GPL-2.0 s.4).
**Court orders:** Conditions imposed by a court, agreement or patent licence do not excuse compliance. If they bar royalty-free redistribution, the bank may not distribute at all (GPL-2.0 s.7).
**Patent licence:** Each contributor grants a royalty-free patent licence under its essential patent claims over its contributor version (GPL-3.0 s.11).

**Knowing reliance:** Where the Corresponding Source is not available to all, a bank relying on a patent licence to convey code must release the source, withdraw its reliance, or extend the patent licence to recipients (GPL-3.0 s.11).
**Downstream recipients:** Each recipient receives a licence automatically. The bank may not add royalties or start patent litigation alleging that the program infringes (GPL-3.0 s.10).
deepDive.takeaway: Treat a compliance letter as a deadline, since the GPL-3.0 s.8 cure clock runs from its receipt.

deepDive.heading: Enforcement and compliance programmes
deepDive.lede: Courts have let copyleft claims proceed, and a compliance programme shows the bank controls its releases.
points: **Conditions:** Jacobsen v. Katzer, 535 F.3d 1373 (Fed. Cir. 2008), held that attribution and change-notice terms were conditions of the licence. A user who broke them could face copyright infringement claims, not only contract claims.
**Contract:** Artifex Software, Inc. v. Hancom, Inc. (N.D. Cal. 2017) refused to dismiss a claim that the GPL is an enforceable contract, on the facts pleaded. The case then settled.

**Third-party beneficiary:** Software Freedom Conservancy v. Vizio, Inc. (Cal. Super. Ct., Orange County, filed October 2021) was brought by a TV buyer claiming, as a third-party beneficiary of the GPL, a right to source code. The court let that theory proceed (reported; check). No final judgment is confirmed as at November 2026 (reported; check).

**Compliance programmes:** OpenChain (ISO/IEC 5230:2020) sets out an open source licence compliance programme, and SPDX (ISO/IEC 5962:2021) provides the licence identifiers, such as GPL-3.0-only, used in this volume (good practice).
**App stores:** VLC was removed from Apple's App Store in January 2011 after a contributor complained that the store's terms conflicted with the GPL (reported; check).
deepDive.takeaway: Answer a compliance letter quickly, with the facts, the source offer and a fix plan.

provisions.title: Modifications and derivative works
provisions.summary: Lets recipients modify the program and distribute the modified work, provided the modified files carry change notices and any work distributed in whole or in part from the program is licensed as a whole at no charge under the GPL. Mere aggregation on a distribution medium does not bring another work under the licence.
provisions.counselNote: This is the core strong copyleft duty. Any product that bundles GPL-2.0 code with bank code needs a boundary analysis before shipment, because the whole distributed work can fall under the licence.

provisions.title: Distribution in object code
provisions.summary: Object code may be distributed only with the corresponding machine-readable source, or with a written offer valid for at least three years to provide it, or, for noncommercial distribution only, with the offer received from upstream. Offering access from a designated place counts as distributing the source if equivalent access is offered for the source.
provisions.counselNote: The source duty is a release obligation. Counsel should require a source offer, the period it runs and a named owner for each shipped GPL-2.0 component.

provisions.title: Termination
provisions.summary: Any attempt to copy, modify, sublicense or distribute the program other than as the licence provides is void and automatically terminates the licensee's rights. Parties who received copies or rights from the licensee keep theirs so long as they remain in full compliance.
provisions.counselNote: The text has no cure period for GPL-2.0, so a breach can end the bank's rights at once. Counsel should treat a compliance problem as urgent even before any notice arrives.

provisions.title: Definitions of modify, propagate and convey
provisions.summary: Defines conveying as any propagation that enables other parties to make or receive copies. Mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not conveying. Propagation covers copying, distribution and making available to the public.
provisions.counselNote: The definition decides when GPL-3.0 duties start. Internal running and remote access without a copy fall outside it, but any transfer of a copy to a third party, including a group company, needs analysis.

provisions.title: Conveying in object code form
provisions.summary: Object code may be conveyed only with the machine-readable Corresponding Source, by one of five listed routes. For a User Product, the Corresponding Source must come with Installation Information where possession and use pass to the recipient in perpetuity or for a fixed term, unless no one retains the ability to install modified object code.
provisions.counselNote: Consumer devices are the trigger to check. A bank that ships a device for personal use may owe installation information, which can conflict with device lock-down and security controls.

provisions.title: Termination and reinstatement
provisions.summary: A licence ends on any propagation or modification outside the licence. It is reinstated provisionally when the violation stops, and permanently if the copyright holder gives no notice within 60 days after the cessation, or if this is the first notice and the violation is cured within 30 days of receipt.
provisions.counselNote: The 30-day cure window is short. Counsel should set up a notice intake so that a letter reaches the legal team on the day it arrives.

provisions.title: Patents
provisions.summary: Each contributor grants a non-exclusive, royalty-free patent licence under its essential patent claims over its contributor version. A conveyor that knowingly relies on a patent licence, where the Corresponding Source is not available to all, must release the source, withdraw its reliance, or extend the licence to downstream recipients.
provisions.counselNote: A bank that contributes to a GPL-3.0 project may grant patent rights through that contribution. Check the patent position of contributions before they are made, and treat a patent assertion against the program as a licence issue.

provisions.instrument: GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1
provisions.title: Combined works using the library
provisions.summary: A work that links with the library may be distributed on the distributor's own terms if those terms permit modification for the customer's own use and reverse engineering for debugging such modifications. The distributor must give notice, supply a copy of the licence, and provide the library source, a shared library mechanism, an offer, or a way to verify receipt.
provisions.counselNote: Under LGPL-2.1, relinking support is the price of proprietary linking. Engineering should confirm that the library can be swapped, and that the terms of the bank's product allow it.

provisions.instrument: GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0
provisions.title: Combined works and installation
provisions.summary: A combined work may be conveyed on terms of the distributor's choice if those terms do not restrict modification of the library portions and reverse engineering for debugging. The distributor must give notices, include the GPL and LGPL texts, and take one of two linking routes: conveying minimal Corresponding Source, or using a suitable shared library mechanism.
provisions.counselNote: LGPL-3.0 adds the GPL texts and linking routes. Confirm which route the product uses, and record it in the release file for each binary.

provisions.title: Distribution of source, executable form and Larger Works
provisions.summary: Covered software distributed in source form stays under the MPL. An executable must be accompanied by a way to obtain the source form at no more than distribution cost. A Larger Work may be distributed on other terms, and covered software in it may take a Secondary License where it is not marked Incompatible With Secondary Licenses.
provisions.counselNote: The MPL is file-level. Counsel should record which files are MPL-covered, and make sure the bank's own code is kept in separate files, because that separation is what keeps the rest of the product outside the licence.

provisions.title: Source distribution and Secondary Licenses
provisions.summary: When the program is distributed as source, it must be made available under the EPL, unless the program is combined with other material in a separate file under a Secondary License and the Exhibit A notice is attached. Secondary License here means the GNU General Public License version 2.0, or a later version of that licence.
provisions.counselNote: An EPL-2.0 component can bring GPL-2.0 terms into a product only where the notice is attached. Engineering should check the header of each file before accepting the component.

provisions.title: Linking with independent modules
provisions.summary: Gives permission to link the covered library with independent modules to produce an executable, regardless of those modules' licence terms, and to distribute the result on terms of the licensee's choice. Modifications to the library may extend the exception, but need not.
provisions.counselNote: The exception is attached to GPL-licensed libraries, so the bank can link them with proprietary modules. It applies only to modules that are not derived from the library, so the boundary must be recorded.

provisions.title: Licence conditions enforceable by copyright claims
provisions.summary: The Federal Circuit held that the attribution and change-notice terms of the Artistic License limited the scope of the licence. A user who broke them was not licensed, so could be sued for copyright infringement and face an injunction, not only for breach of contract.
provisions.counselNote: Open source conditions can carry copyright remedies. The bank's release and attribution failures can therefore be framed as infringement, which affects insurance and disclosure decisions.

provisions.instrument: Artifex Software, Inc. v. Hancom, Inc.
provisions.title: GPL as an enforceable contract
provisions.summary: The court refused to dismiss a claim that the GPL is an enforceable contract, on the facts pleaded. The defendant had used the Ghostscript program under the GPL without complying and without a commercial licence. The case then settled.
provisions.counselNote: A pleading decision, not a final judgment, but it shows that a GPL claim can proceed as a contract claim as well as a copyright claim. Counsel should expect both theories in a dispute.

checklist: **Inventory every copyleft component** with its SPDX identifier, version, the products that convey it and its linking pattern, drawn from the software bill of materials.
**Set a release gate:** Block any build that conveys GPL, LGPL, MPL or EPL code until the source offer, notices and licence texts are in place.

**Publish a source offer** with each binary, or, under GPL-2.0 or for a GPL-3.0 physical product, a written offer valid for at least three years, and keep the source available for as long as the offer runs.
**Record the boundary** of each work: where copyleft code is linked or combined with bank code, and engineering sign-off on that design.
**Keep notices intact:** Retain licence headers and the licence text with each copy, and do not strip per-file notices.
**Treat internal copies with care:** Confirm that no copy leaves the bank or its group, and record the group-company position as a documented policy choice.
**Check for consumer devices:** Identify any product sold for personal or household use, because GPL-3.0 s.6 installation information duties then apply.
**Calendar the cure clock:** On a notice that is the first from that copyright holder, start the 30-day GPL-3.0 s.8 window at once and inform the legal team the same day.
**Agree a response protocol** for compliance letters, with a named owner, the facts, the source offer, a fix plan and one point of contact.
**Register exceptions and secondary licences** for each component, so the terms that apply to each file are known before release.
itAngle: **Scanner output:** Licence scanners detect copyleft headers, but a match does not show whether code is linked, dynamically loaded or run as a separate process. Engineering must confirm the architecture (good practice).

**Linking map:** Record whether each library is statically or dynamically linked into each binary. Relinking under LGPL-3.0 needs a shared library mechanism or the minimal Corresponding Source (LGPL-3.0 s.4(d)).

**Build pipeline:** Make the build produce the source archive and the written offer alongside the binary. Corresponding Source includes the scripts that control compilation and installation (GPL-3.0 s.1).

**Dependency updates:** A routine package update can add copyleft code to a permissive product. Gate dependency changes so that a new GPL, LGPL, MPL or EPL component is reviewed before it merges (good practice).
**App store terms:** Store terms that restrict redistribution can conflict with copyleft licences, as the reported VLC removal from Apple's App Store in 2011 shows (reported; check).
virtualBankNotes: **Vendor SDKs:** Mobile or vendor SDKs shipped inside bank apps can carry copyleft obligations to every customer who receives the app, so vendor warranties on open source components matter (drafting inference).
**Customer devices:** Branded hardware sold to personal customers, such as card readers, can be a User Product, which brings installation information duties under GPL-3.0 s.6.

**Fintech partners:** When a bank opens APIs or SDKs to fintech partners, copyleft conveying rules apply to any code the partner receives. Partner terms should include the source offer where copyleft code is in the SDK (good practice).

**Vendor oversight:** The interagency third-party guidance (88 Fed. Reg. 37920) is technology-neutral and does not deal with open source as such, so copyleft compliance sits in vendor contracts and the bank's own release controls (drafting inference).
**Examiner evidence:** Examiners ask for software inventories and vendor evidence. A copyleft register and a documented release gate show that the bank controls what it ships (good practice).
productNotes: **Say where copyleft code meets the bank's code:** Tell counsel which parts of the product use GPL, LGPL, MPL or EPL code and how they are linked. A distributed combined work may have to carry the GPL as a whole (GPL-2.0 s.2(b); GPL-3.0 s.5(c)).

**Ask who receives a copy:** Running GPL code inside the bank is generally not conveying, but a copy sent to an affiliate, contractor or partner can be. Tell counsel before the code leaves the bank or its group (GPL-3.0 s.0; drafting inference).

**Put the source offer on the release checklist:** Each binary that goes out with GPL-2.0 code needs its source with it or a written offer valid for at least three years (GPL-2.0 s.3(a), (b)). Under GPL-3.0 a written offer is available only for a physical product (GPL-3.0 s.6(b)); a download needs the source with it or access to it from a designated place (GPL-3.0 s.6(d)). Book that offer into the launch plan (good practice).

**Flag personal devices and partner SDKs:** Branded hardware sold to personal or household customers, such as card readers, may bring GPL-3.0 installation information duties where possession and use pass to the buyer (GPL-3.0 s.6). An SDK given to partners can carry copyleft duties to each recipient (drafting inference).
pitfalls: **Assuming internal use is free:** Internal running is generally not conveying, but a copy sent to an affiliate, contractor or partner can be (GPL-3.0 s.0; drafting inference).
**Shipping without source:** Distributing GPL-2.0 binaries with neither the source nor a written offer breaches GPL-2.0 s.3, and the licence then ends under s.4.
**Silent linking:** Static linking or plugin loading that the team does not record can turn a library into a combined work the bank has not assessed.
**Slow reply to a notice:** Under GPL-3.0 s.8, a licensee who is first notified must cure within 30 days of receipt to be permanently reinstated, so a slow reply can cost the bank that reinstatement.
**Treating the FSF view as law:** The FSF's view that linking creates a combined work has not been adopted by any US court, and should not be presented as settled.

points: **Licence terms cannot cut back interoperability:** contract terms that override the rights to observe, study or test a program, or to decompile for interoperability, are void (Directive 2009/24/EC, Art. 8; see Arts. 5(3), 6).
**National courts have heard GPL claims:** Welte v. Sitecom (Germany, 2004) and Entr'ouvert v. Orange (France, 2024) are the reference cases, while Hellwig v. VMware was dismissed (reported; check).
**Same copyright footing:** programs are literary works (CDPA 1988 s.3(1)(b)), so a copyleft licence rests on the same copyright and contract base as in the US.
**Lawful-user rights:** back-up copies, decompilation and observe-study-test are permitted (CDPA 1988 ss.50A-50C), so check any copyleft or licence term that limits them against those sections.
**Lawful-user rights:** owners or licensees of a program may adapt it for compatibility and make back-up copies (Copyright Act s.30.6), and may reproduce it for interoperability (s.30.61).
**Contract, not statute:** Canada has no general open source statute, so copyleft terms are enforced as contract or through copyright (Copyright Act, C-42).

hongKong.summary: Under Hong Kong copyright, a copyleft licence is the permission for the restricted acts, chiefly issuing copies to the public and making adaptations, and its main duties start when copies go to others, so the bank's distribution and modification choices decide the scope. The main difference from the US is that Hong Kong has no general fair use and no express decompilation right, so reverse engineering rests on the lawful-user rules and on the licence itself (Cap. 528 ss.22(1)(a), (g), 37, 61).
keyPoints: **Who can license:** The bank can put its own code under a copyleft licence only if it owns the copyright. Code written by an employee in the course of employment belongs to the employer (Cap. 528 s.14(1)), and commissioned code belongs to the contractor unless the contract expressly gives the copyright to the bank (Cap. 528 ss.13, 15(1)), though the bank always has an exclusive licence to exploit it for the purposes contemplated at commissioning (Cap. 528 s.15(2)(a)).

**Trigger:** Copyleft duties attach to conveying, which GPL-3.0 defines by reference to the acts copyright law restricts (GPL-3.0 s.0; Cap. 528 ss.22-29). Running software inside the bank is not conveying (GPL-3.0 s.0).

**Lawful users:** A user with a contractual right to use a program may make a back-up copy unless the agreement says otherwise (Cap. 528 s.60(3)), and may copy or adapt it where necessary for lawful use, including to correct errors (Cap. 528 ss.60(1)-(2), 61(1)-(2)).

**No decompilation right:** The Ordinance has no express decompilation or interoperability exception. Reverse engineering for interoperability is excused only in narrow cases, under the circumvention exception and the lawful-user rules (Cap. 528 s.273D(1); s.61).
**Breach:** Once a copyleft licence stops authorising a use, further copying or adapting infringes copyright, and the owner may claim damages and injunctions (Cap. 528 ss.22-24, 29, 107(1)-(2)).

sections.heading: Scope: what Hong Kong copyright makes the trigger
sections.lede: The copyleft duty follows the acts that copyright restricts, so the bank must map each copy and each adaptation.
points: **Restricted acts:** Copying, issuing copies to the public, communicating to the public and making adaptations are restricted, and each needs a licence or a permitted act (Cap. 528 ss.22(1), 23(1)-(2), 29(1)).
**Storage counts:** Storing a work in any medium by electronic means is copying, so each internal copy on a build server, container image or repository is a restricted act (Cap. 528 s.23(2)).
**Adaptations:** A modified version is an adaptation, and for a program an adaptation includes an altered version or a translation into another language or code (Cap. 528 s.29(3)(b), (4)).

**Linking:** No Hong Kong ruling on whether linking creates a work based on another is reported (reported; check). The statutory test turns on whether a substantial part is copied or an adaptation is made (Cap. 528 ss.22(3), 29(3)(b)).

**Joint work:** Where contractor and bank staff collaborate so that their contributions are not distinct, the work is jointly authored, and the Ordinance refers to all the joint authors together (Cap. 528 s.12(1), (4)). Clear each contributor's rights before a copyleft release (good practice).
sections.takeaway: Map each copy and adaptation of copyleft code, and clear each contributor's rights, before deciding which licence applies.

sections.heading: Lawful users and reverse engineering
sections.lede: The statute gives a lawful user some room, but no general right to take a program apart.
points: **Who is a lawful user:** A person with a contractual right to use the program (Cap. 528 s.60(2)). For offences under s.118(1), that right can be in any place in or outside Hong Kong (Cap. 528 s.118A(a)).
**Back-up copies:** A lawful user may make a back-up copy that is necessary for lawful use, but an agreement to the contrary can exclude that right (Cap. 528 s.60(1), (3)).

**Adaptation for lawful use:** A lawful user may copy or adapt where necessary for lawful use, including to correct errors (Cap. 528 s.61(1)-(2)). The section has no express words allowing an agreement to exclude it, so whether a licence can cut it back is a question of construction (drafting inference).

**Interoperability:** Circumventing a technological measure on a program for the sole purpose of interoperability is excused only if the element analysed is not readily available to the person, the sole purpose is interoperability with an independently created program, the copy is not infringing, and the analysis is not itself an infringement (Cap. 528 s.273D(1)(b)-(e)). The exception covers circumvention, not copying or adapting.
**Licence permission:** Reverse engineering for debugging is a licence permission, as in LGPL-2.1 s.6 and LGPL-3.0 s.4, not a statutory right (drafting inference).
sections.takeaway: Check each copyleft and vendor licence for a reverse-engineering permission before engineering starts, because the statute will not supply one.

sections.heading: Breach, termination and remedies
sections.lede: Copying outside the licence infringes, and the owner has remedies that go beyond damages.
points: **Primary infringement:** Copying or adapting without a licence infringes, and no knowledge requirement applies to that primary infringement (Cap. 528 s.22(2)).

**Secondary infringement:** Importing or exporting, possessing for trade, selling or distributing an infringing copy needs knowledge or reason to believe that the copy is infringing (Cap. 528 ss.30, 31(1)-(2)).

**Remedies:** The owner may claim damages, injunctions and accounts (Cap. 528 s.107(1)-(2)). Additional damages may be awarded for flagrancy, benefit to the defendant, conduct and wide circulation (Cap. 528 s.108(2)). Damages are barred only where the defendant did not know, and had no reason to believe, that copyright subsisted in the work (Cap. 528 s.108(1)).

**Business offence:** Possessing an unlicensed copy of a program for the purpose of or in the course of a trade or business, with a view to its being used by any person for that business, is an offence, subject to the defences in s.118(3) to (3B) (Cap. 528 s.118(2A)-(2B)). On indictment the penalty is a level 5 fine per copy and 4 years' imprisonment (Cap. 528 s.118(2A), s.119(1)).
**Officers:** A director or manager commits the offence too if the company's offence was committed with their consent or connivance, or is attributable to them (Cap. 528 s.125(1)).
**Licence ends:** Continued copying or adapting outside the licence is infringement, so record the date a licence ends and remediate before the owner asks (good practice).
**No local ruling:** No reported Hong Kong decision enforces a copyleft licence, so the bank should rely on the licence text and on each contributor's copyright (reported; check).
sections.takeaway: When a copyleft licence ends or is breached, treat later copying as unlicensed and remediate it promptly.

provisions.title: Acts restricted by copyright
provisions.summary: The owner has the exclusive right to copy the work, issue copies to the public, communicate it to the public and make an adaptation, and to do those acts in relation to an adaptation. Doing a restricted act without licence infringes.
provisions.counselNote: Each copy the bank makes or issues of copyleft code is a restricted act, so the licence is the only permission unless a statutory exception applies.

provisions.title: Copying includes electronic storage
provisions.summary: Copying means reproducing the work in any material form, and storing it in any medium by electronic means counts as copying.
provisions.counselNote: Loading copyleft code into a build server, container image or repository is copying, so each internal copy needs a licence even if nothing is shipped.

provisions.title: Adaptations
provisions.summary: Making an adaptation of a literary work is restricted, and so is doing a restricted act in relation to an adaptation. For a program, an adaptation includes an altered version or a translation.
provisions.counselNote: A modified or ported copyleft program is an adaptation, so it needs the licence's permission when it is made. GPL-3.0 gives that permission without conditions for copies the bank does not convey (GPL-3.0 s.2).

provisions.title: Dealing with infringing copies
provisions.summary: Possessing for trade or business, selling or hiring, exhibiting, distributing and related acts infringe if the person knows or has reason to believe that the copy is infringing.
provisions.counselNote: A bank that receives third-party code in breach of its licence is not caught by s.31 unless it knows or has reason to believe the copy is infringing (drafting inference).

provisions.title: Lawful user back-up copy
provisions.summary: A lawful user, meaning a person with a contractual right to use the program, may make a back-up copy where that is necessary for lawful use. An agreement to the contrary can override this section.
provisions.counselNote: A vendor licence can exclude the back-up right, so read the terms before relying on it.

provisions.title: Lawful user copying and adapting
provisions.summary: A lawful user may copy or adapt a program where that is necessary for lawful use, including to correct errors. The section has no express words allowing an agreement to exclude it.
provisions.counselNote: This is the main statutory basis for adapting a licensed program, but whether a licence can cut it back is a question of construction (drafting inference).

provisions.title: Circumventing technological measures
provisions.summary: Circumventing an effective technological measure on a copyright work is actionable where the person knows or has reason to believe that he is circumventing it, subject to the exceptions in ss.273D and 273H. The owner and exclusive licensees have copyright-type remedies.
provisions.counselNote: A licence key or other measure on a copyleft-based product brings this section into play, so check the s.273D exceptions before any workaround (good practice).

provisions.title: Interoperability exception
provisions.summary: Circumvention is excused only where all of the statutory conditions are met: the act identifies or analyses program elements not readily available to the person, it is done for the sole purpose of interoperability with an independently created program, the copy is not infringing, and the analysis is not itself an infringement. The copy must not be infringing, and the analysis must not itself be an infringement. The exception does not cover copying or adapting.
provisions.counselNote: This is the only statutory route to circumvent for interoperability, and it is narrow, so engineering should not assume that a licence permission removes the copyright limits (drafting inference).

bankNotes: **Customer apps:** Issuing copies to the public is a restricted act (Cap. 528 s.22(1)(b)), so an app built on GPL-3.0 code and given to customers must come with its Corresponding Source in one of the ways GPL-3.0 s.6 allows; for a download, that means equivalent access to the source through the same place, or on another server that clear directions point to (GPL-3.0 s.6(d)). The written-offer route is only for object code in a physical product (GPL-3.0 s.6(b)).

**Vendor contracts:** The HKMA's outsourcing guideline (SA-2) expects written agreements with vendors. Guidance is not law, but ownership, open source warranty and audit terms belong in each contract (good practice).

**Personal data in code:** Personal data in released code or test data is a risk under DPP 4(1), and reusing it for a new purpose needs the data subject's prescribed consent under DPP 3(1) (Cap. 486 Sch. 1, DPP 3(1), DPP 4(1); drafting inference).

glossary.definition: A licence model under which distributed works based on the licensed code must carry the same terms. Strong copyleft (GPL) covers the whole work; weak copyleft (LGPL, MPL, EPL) covers the library or the file (LGPL-2.1 s.6; MPL-2.0 s.3.3).
GPL-3.0's term for propagation that enables others to make or receive copies. Mere interaction with a user over a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not conveying (GPL-3.0 s.0).
All source code needed to generate, install and run the object code and to modify the work, including control scripts. It excludes System Libraries and general tools used unmodified (GPL-3.0 s.1).
A consumer product, meaning tangible personal property normally used for personal, family or household purposes, or a product designed or sold for incorporation into a dwelling (GPL-3.0 s.6).
The methods, procedures, authorization keys or other information needed to install and run modified versions of a covered work on a User Product (GPL-3.0 s.6).
A work that combines Covered Software with other material in a separate file or files, where the other material is not Covered Software (MPL-2.0 s.1.7).
For MPL-2.0, the GNU General Public License 2.0, the GNU Lesser General Public License 2.1, the GNU Affero General Public License 3.0, or later versions of those licences (MPL-2.0 s.1.12).
An additional permission to the GPL that lets independent modules link with the covered library and keep their own licence terms (Classpath-exception-2.0).
The ISO/IEC 5230:2020 standard for open source licence compliance programmes, which sets out the requirements a programme must meet.

A person with a contractual right to use a computer program. A lawful user may make back-up copies unless the agreement says otherwise (Cap. 528 s.60(1), (3)), and may copy or adapt the program where necessary for lawful use (Cap. 528 s.61(1)).

title: Network copyleft and source-available licences
oneLiner: A network licence can bind the bank without any distribution, and source-available terms can tighten after the bank has adopted the code.
keyPoints: Network use can create a duty: a modified AGPL-3.0 program that remote users interact with must offer them its source, even if the bank never distributes it (AGPL-3.0 s.13).
**Unmodified use:** Running an unmodified AGPL-3.0 program over a network triggers nothing under s.13, and the licence expressly affirms unlimited permission to run it (AGPL-3.0 s.2).

**Not open source:** [[Source-available|source-available]] licences such as SSPL, BUSL, Elastic License 2.0 and the Commons Clause show the code but limit its use, so policy must not file them as open source (reported; check).

**Licence changes:** Several database and infrastructure vendors moved from AGPL-3.0, permissive or weak copyleft licences to source-available terms between 2018 and 2025, and some later added AGPL-3.0 as an option (reported; check).
**Released code:** A licence change normally applies to later versions, so code already received under the earlier terms keeps them (drafting inference; check each licence's wording).
**Counsel's role:** Inventory network-facing components, read each licence's network and change terms, and write vendor clauses that require notice of changes and provide a fallback (good practice).

deepDive.heading: Network use can create a duty
deepDive.lede: The AGPL reaches software that is never handed over.

visual.caption: The duty depends on whether the program is modified and whether users reach it remotely, not on who the users are.

items.note: No duty under s.13

items.label: Modify
items.note: Adapting the program makes a modified version

items.label: Serve remote users
items.note: Interaction over a network is not conveying

points: **Trigger:** If you modify the program, your modified version must prominently offer everyone interacting with it remotely through a computer network an opportunity to receive its Corresponding Source (AGPL-3.0 s.13).

**No conveying:** Mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not [[conveying|Conveying]] (AGPL-3.0 s.0). The network duty therefore applies without any distribution.
**Unmodified use:** The licence grants unlimited permission to run the unmodified program, and running it over a network triggers nothing under s.13 (AGPL-3.0 s.2).
**Users:** The text does not confine the offer to outside customers, so staff or partners who use a modified service remotely are probably users too (drafting inference).
**Scope:** The Corresponding Source includes the source needed to generate, install, run and modify the work, including the scripts that control those activities (AGPL-3.0 s.1).

deepDive.heading: Source-available is not open source
deepDive.lede: Several licences show the code while limiting what the bank may do with it.

visual.caption: Summary only. Read each licence text before relying on it (reported; check).

items.note: Source offer for modified network use (s.13)

items.note: Service source for services offered to others (reported; check)
